title: Looping over lists
summary: Visit every item with for, add them up with sum, find the smallest and biggest, and build new lists inside a loop.

intro.text:
A `for` loop works on a list just like it did on text and `range`. Each round, the loop name gets the **next item**:

```
for price in prices:
    total += price
```

No positions needed. The **cells** panel shows a pointer moving from box to box.

Some totals are so common that Python has them built in:

- `sum(xs)` adds up all the numbers
- `min(xs)` and `max(xs)` find the smallest and the biggest
- the average is `sum(xs) / len(xs)`

To **build a new list**, start with an empty one before the loop and `append` inside it, often behind an `if` so only some items are kept.

Slices work on lists too, and give back a new list: `xs[1:]` is everything but the first item, `xs[:3]` the first three. Loop over a slice to skip items.
intro.analogy: A conveyor belt at a checkout. Each item rolls past the scanner once, in order, and the scanner can add up the price or set some items aside in a new bag.

quiz.q: How many rounds does `for x in [3, 6]:` run?
quiz.why: One round per item, and the list has 2 items.
sum adds up all the items.
Strings compare letter by letter, so the biggest is the one that comes last in the alphabet.
A slice of a list is a new list, from position 1 up to (not including) 3.

quiz.q: You build a new list inside a loop with append. Where does `result = []` go?
quiz.why: Inside the loop it would start empty again every round.

quiz.q: With `xs = [10, 20]`, what does `for i in xs: print(xs[i])` do?
quiz.why: i is the item itself (10), not a position. There is no position 10.

mistakes.title: Using the item as a position
mistakes.explain: p already is the item: 10, then 20. Asking for prices[10] looks for a position that does not exist. Just use p.

mistakes.title: The average of an empty list
mistakes.explain: An empty list has a length of 0, and dividing by 0 has no answer. Check that the list has items first.

mistakes.title: Adding up numbers stored as text
mistakes.explain: sum only adds numbers. Text that looks like a number is still text. Turn each item into an int first.
